title: random_init_baseline silently reshuffles training data via the global RNG
description: After per-seed seeding (L964-965) and construction of the real model (L971), random_init_baseline calls torch.manual_seed(cfg.seed+1000+s) and builds 3 more models, leaving the GLOBAL torch generator at a state that depends on the model's parameter count. Training is not re-seeded before T1 (L997), and DataLoader(shuffle=True) draws its per-epoch shuffle from that global generator. So training data order - and every trained accuracy - is coupled to the baseline routine: change n_seeds, shared_dim, num_patterns, or add a layer and the main result moves with no other edit. Inherited by run_cl_confirmation_fixed.py (call L212) and run_cl_rehearsal.py (call L187).
evidence: def L804-823; torch.manual_seed L812; called L983; no re-seed before T1 train L997
fix: Snapshot/restore RNG around the baseline (state=torch.get_rng_state() ... torch.set_rng_state(state)), or build baseline models with a local torch.Generator, and re-seed torch.manual_seed(cfg.seed) immediately before T1.

title: 'fwt' means two different things; the aggregated one is not forward transfer
description: In m7_trimodal_run.py the T2 head is untrained at the zero-shot eval (L559), so acc_t2_zero_shot ~ chance and fwt = post_train - chance is a LEARNING GAIN, not forward transfer. The provenance file computes genuine FWT (zero_shot - random_init, L1066, stored T2_fwt). The canonical loader aggregates the column literally named 'fwt' (load_results.py L206), i.e. the mislabeled learning-gain. A headline 'forward transfer ~75pp' sourced this way measures 'training on T2 helps T2', which is trivial and contradicts the correspondence-paper narrative (FWT~0).
evidence: m7 L616 fwt=acc_t2_after_t2-acc_t2_zero_shot stored 'fwt' L630 vs provenance L1066 fwt_t2=acc_t2_zero_shot-random_init_baselines[task2]
fix: Rename m7_trimodal_run.py's quantity to learning_gain; compute true FWT as zero_shot - random_init_baseline (as provenance does) if forward transfer is the claim; align the canonical loader's aggregated column.

title: Results CSV append-without-dedup; provenance aggregator never dedups
description: m7_trimodal_run.py _save_incremental (L687-697) reuses metric_name as BOTH the step value AND a populated column (L690) so T1_after_T1/T2_after_T2/T3_after_T3 appear in both incremental and summary rows; summary write L634-640 appends with no dedup. provenance save_seed_result L849-860 appends with no dedup; aggregate_results filters notna (L885, good) but never drop_duplicates, then computes mean/std(ddof=1)/n=len(sub)/ci95 (L894-905) and a Wilcoxon set_index('seed') (L913-915). A rerun (routine, because checkpoint-skip re-evaluates) appends a second summary row per seed: n inflates, std/ci95 collapse, the Wilcoxon join explodes on duplicate seed indices, and m7's naive reader gets different n per metric.
fix: Route all analysis through load_results.py (aggregates over unique seeds). In aggregate_results add df=df[df.get('step').isna()].drop_duplicates(['seed','condition'],keep='last') before aggregation. In _save_incremental stop reusing metric_name as the column name.

title: Checkpoint-skip has no staleness/config guard; provenance filename is config-blind
description: m7 L537-539/563-565/590-592 and provenance L993-995/1042-1044/1094-1096 skip training when a matching-named checkpoint exists, with no warning. Filename final_{task}_{task}_seed{seed}_{condition}.pt (provenance L992) is keyed only by task/seed/condition, NOT by shared_dim, num_patterns, or align_*. If architecture/loss changes, a stale old checkpoint is loaded and evaluated as fresh; an ablation that flips align_cross_modal or changes shared_dim reuses a different-config checkpoint. run_cl_confirmation_fixed._is_complete_result (L53-60) skips a whole recompute purely because the CSV has expected columns. On skip, _save_gate_history is not written, so Figure 3 silently loses those seeds.
evidence: save bare {'model_state_dict'} m7 L543/571/598; provenance filename L992
fix: Embed {config_hash, git_sha, code_version} in the checkpoint; on load verify it matches and retrain on mismatch; put a config hash in the filename; gate _is_complete_result on the same hash.

title: Accuracy computed and stored everywhere without spike rate / sparsity / timestep count
description: evaluate returns only 100*correct/total (m7 L410-419; provenance L539-548) and result dicts carry only accuracy-derived metrics (m7 L618-631; provenance L1137-1159; joint scripts too). The backbones build spike tensors then sum them away (m7 L271, audio L318). This directly violates the 'accuracy never travels alone' rule: the model computes spikes but never records firing rate/sparsity, and no timestep count travels with the number, so the SynOps/energy story has no in-repo source and every reported accuracy is the flattering half.
evidence: evaluate m7 L410-419 / provenance L539-548 return accuracy only
fix: Have evaluate/train_task also return mean spikes-per-neuron-per-timestep (from spk_rec, e.g. spk.mean()), sparsity, and T; write them into the same result row/CSV alongside every accuracy.

title: SHD runs 100 timesteps while N-MNIST/DVS run 25; time_steps=25 misrepresents SHD; ~4x feature-magnitude asymmetry into the shared gate
description: SHD events_to_dense uses time_bins=100 (m7 L139; provenance L1201; and confirmation/rehearsal/joint files) while visual/DVS collates clamp to 25 (m7 L77-80/94-97) and CONFIG['time_steps']=25 (m7 L58). Features are a SUM over T (m7 L271/318). So the audio backbone integrates over 100 steps and visual over 25: time_steps=25 is false for SHD (any reported timestep count would be wrong, and the SpiNNaker beta=exp(-dt/tau) mapping is off for audio), and SHD embeddings feed the shared, non-normalized adaptive_gate (m7 L295-296) at ~4x the magnitude of visual embeddings, coupling gate/Hopfield behaviour to the step-count asymmetry.
evidence: events_to_dense time_bins=100 vs collate clamp 25 vs CONFIG time_steps=25
fix: Either bin SHD to 25 (respect time_steps) or record the true per-modality T and report it; if the asymmetry is intentional, state it and normalize features before the gate.

title: Training DataLoaders shuffle from the global RNG (no per-loader generator=)
description: Every shuffle=True training loader omits generator= (m7 L127; provenance L1187/1191; confirmation L88; rehearsal L66; run_joint_shared_encoder L438). With no dedicated generator, RandomSampler seeds each epoch's shuffle from the global torch generator, whose state is whatever model construction (and SNN-001) left it. Any change to init order or parameter count reshuffles the training stream and moves trained numbers even with the same seed. This is the general mechanism SNN-001 exploits.
evidence: m7 L127 DataLoader(...,shuffle=True) with no generator=
fix: Pass generator=torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed) to each training DataLoader so shuffling is decoupled from init RNG (mirrors how the splits are already pinned).

title: Provenance config JSON records max_epochs=50/patience=12 but the run hardcodes 15/5
description: ExperimentConfig.max_epochs=50, patience=12 (L41-42) are saved next to the checkpoint (cfg.to_json L1005), but train_task is called with num_epochs=15, patience=5 (L999/1047/1099). The provenance edition's whole purpose is faithful config capture, yet the persisted JSON misstates the training length actually used. Separately m7 hardcodes weight_decay=1e-4 (L424) ignoring CONFIG['weight_decay'], and dropout=0.2 (L53) and pin_memory (L59) are never used.
evidence: provenance L41-42 vs call L999; m7 L424 vs CONFIG
fix: Pass cfg.max_epochs/cfg.patience into train_task (or set them to 15/5 so the JSON is truthful); replace the hardcoded 1e-4 in m7 with CONFIG['weight_decay']; drop or wire the unused keys.

title: best_*.pt is saved but the reported metric uses last-epoch (post-early-stop) weights
description: best checkpoint is saved on val improvement (L485-495), early stop breaks patience epochs later (L496-500), but the reported test_acc evaluates the CURRENT (degraded) weights (L504, again L545); best_*.pt is never reloaded. provenance reports last-epoch (L671) and saves no best. The reported test accuracy is from a model up to patience=5 epochs past its best validation, so the paper number is systematically off the intended best model and the saved best_*.pt is a red herring. Magnitude is data-dependent and unmeasured.
evidence: best saved L485-495, never reloaded; test on current weights L504
fix: Reload best_*.pt before the final evaluate, or state explicitly that the reported model is the final (early-stopped) one and remove the unused best checkpoint.

title: forgetting_T1_T3 is the incremental (T2->T3) drop, not total forgetting
description: m7 L614 and provenance L1134: forgetting_T1_T3 = acc_t1_after_t2 - acc_t1_after_t3. The name implies total T1 forgetting after T3 (from its post-T1 peak) but measures only the T3-induced increment. run_cl_confirmation_fixed.py L329 correctly adds total_forgetting_T1_T3 = acc_t1_after - acc_t1_after_t3. RULE 5 makes the forgetting number load-bearing, so a reviewer aggregating this as total forgetting understates it.
evidence: m7 L613-614; provenance L1133-1134; contrast confirmation L329
fix: Rename to forgetting_T1_dueto_T3 (incremental) and add an explicit total_forgetting_T1_T3 as in the confirmation script.

title: Provenance runs 5 seeds (incl. 101112), not the policy [42,123,456]; three inconsistent seed sets across scripts
description: provenance seeds=[42,123,456,789,101112] (L63, used L1320) vs m7 SEEDS=[42,123,456] (L516). Joint scripts use ...,789,1011 (run_joint_magnitude_ablation L62; run_joint_shared_encoder L85). The two 'M7' entrypoints aggregate over different n (5 vs 3) so their mean+/-std are not comparable, and provenance violates the documented seed policy the loader enforces (load_results.py L156-163). 101112 vs 1011 looks like a typo that fragments cross-script comparability.
evidence: provenance L63 seeds list; m7 L516
fix: Set provenance seeds=[42,123,456]; reconcile the joint scripts' fifth seed with the intended value.

title: run_cl_rehearsal.py prints a comparison table built from hardcoded result literals
description: L435-444 hardcode literals (97.21, 97.50, 54.85, 15.33, 79.64, 78.41, -0.08, 37.41, 84.20, 36.92, 14.80, 0.59, 0.21) printed next to fresh res[...] values, producing a table that looks coherent but is half fabricated (97.21/79.64 match the contested single-task numbers). Same pattern that made the figures untrustworthy; violates RULE 1.
evidence: L435-444 literals
fix: Load baseline columns from their CSVs, or print only freshly computed values and clearly mark any external reference as unsourced.

title: Two divergent M7 entrypoints produce non-comparable numbers
description: m7_trimodal_run.py vs m7_trimodal_run_provenance.py differ in RNG order (SNN-001), fwt/forgetting definitions (SNN-002/010), CSV schema (SNN-003), and seed count (SNN-011). CLAUDE.md names m7_trimodal_run.py the entrypoint and the canonical loader matches its schema, yet every run_* script imports the provenance hub - so it is ambiguous which file produced any published number, and the two are not numerically interchangeable.
evidence: schema/metric/seed differences enumerated across SNN-001/002/003/010/011
fix: Declare one source-of-record, have the other import from it (no duplicated run_one_seed/model code), and reconcile metric definitions.

title: torch.mps.manual_seed set in joint scripts but not in entrypoint/hub; dropout=0.2 declared but unused
description: No MPS seed in m7 (L523-524) or provenance (L964-965); the joint scripts do call torch.mps.manual_seed (run_joint_shared_encoder L767-768; run_joint_magnitude_ablation L763-764). dropout=0.2 (m7 L53 / provenance L45) is never used. Currently inert for the entrypoint (init is on CPU before .to(device), no MPS stochastic op), so results are reproducible today - but wiring the declared dropout would introduce forward-time MPS RNG the entrypoint does not seed, silently breaking reproducibility.
evidence: joint scripts seed MPS; entrypoints do not; dropout unused
fix: Add torch.mps.manual_seed(seed) in both entrypoints for parity, or remove the unused dropout key so it cannot be wired without review.

title: Python random never seeded; joint-encoder split policy diverges
description: Python's random is never seeded (m7 L523-524; provenance L964-965) - inert only because random is not imported/used, but a gap the moment any stdlib-random call is added. Separately run_joint_shared_encoder.py pins its train/val split with manual_seed(seed) (L435) so the split moves with seed - divergent from the M7 policy of manual_seed(42) (defensible for that standalone experiment, but worth stating).
evidence: no random.seed; joint split manual_seed(seed) L435
fix: Add random.seed(seed) alongside torch/numpy seeds; document the joint-encoder split policy.

title: VERIFIED-CORRECT: num_workers=0 is respected everywhere (do not 'optimize')
description: num_workers=0 is a literal everywhere (m7 L127-132; provenance L1187; confirmation L88; rehearsal L66); run_joint_shared_encoder routes through cfg.num_workers (L440) defaulting 0. This is REQUIRED on macOS (tonic multiprocessing does not survive fork) and is not a performance knob. Recorded so a fixing agent does not raise it.
evidence: num_workers=0 literals across M7-lineage files
fix: Do NOT change. Leave num_workers=0 on macOS/MPS.

title: VERIFIED-CORRECT: reported accuracy uses the TEST split, not validation
description: evaluate is called on test_loader_* for every reported accuracy (m7 L545/573/600; provenance L1007/1057/1109); best_val is used only for early-stop model selection. RULE 4 (report test, not validation) is satisfied - subject only to the best-vs-last caveat in SNN-009.
evidence: evaluate(test_loader_*) at the cited lines
fix: No change needed; keep reporting the test split.

title: VERIFIED-CORRECT: dataset splits are pinned across seeds with a LOCAL generator
description: Splits use torch.Generator().manual_seed(42) in all M7-lineage files (m7 L126/154/172; provenance L1185/1217/1238; confirmation L86/118/139; rehearsal L64/96/117). Splits do not vary by seed - only init/shuffle do, as intended. This is a LOCAL generator so it does not perturb the global RNG (contrast SNN-001/007 which are about the global RNG driving shuffle).
evidence: torch.Generator().manual_seed(42) at the split sites
fix: No change needed; this is the correct split-pinning pattern.

title: VERIFIED-CORRECT: beta=0.9 applied uniformly to every LIF neuron
description: beta=0.9 is applied uniformly to every snn.Leaky (m7 L238-247/283-289; provenance via cfg.beta); it is not a per-layer knob and no code path overrides it - consistent with the SpiNNaker tau_m mapping the docs rely on.
evidence: snn.Leaky(beta=0.9) uniform
fix: No change needed; keep beta uniform.

title: VERIFIED-CORRECT: no silent MPS CPU-fallback env is set
description: PYTORCH_ENABLE_MPS_FALLBACK appears in none of the audited training files; the numpy svd / adaptive_avg_pool2d paths run on CPU by construction, not via hidden fallback. So there is no undisclosed CPU fallback changing timing or numerics.
evidence: no PYTORCH_ENABLE_MPS_FALLBACK anywhere in the training files
fix: No change needed; do not set the fallback env without disclosing it.
